angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 402,115 km at 91.07 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.9803 +/- 0.0135 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 91.07 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.578 +/- 0.028 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-147 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 402,115 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.563 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-147 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3690 +/- 300 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-147 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-147 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-147.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.665, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
